advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_open_blockers` use `_get_ticket_status` (tombstone/missing-dir aware) so the reported blocker set matches `build_dep_graph`'s `ready_to_work` rule, or correct the docstring claim.
evidence: claimability.py:88 docstring: "the same open-vs-closed rule ``build_dep_graph`` uses to compute ``ready_to_work``"
claimability.py:95-99: `st = reduce_ticket(os.path.join(tracker, bid)) or {}` … `if str(st.get("status", "")) not in ("closed", "deleted"): open_ids.append(bid)`
src/rebar/graph/_graph.py:105-108: `status = _get_ticket_status(blocker_id, tracker_dir)` … `if status not in ("closed", "deleted")` — uses _get_ticket_status, not raw reduce_ticket

src/rebar/graph/_status.py:31-42: `_get_ticket_status` returns "closed" for a missing directory and reads `.tombstone.json` status; src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:170-171 shows `reduce_ticket` returns None (not those states) when a dir has no event files
advisory.finding: `_open_blockers` recomputes each blocker's open/closed status with raw `reduce_ticket`, which diverges from `build_dep_graph`'s tombstone/missing-dir-aware `_get_ticket_status`: a blocker whose directory is missing (archived-away) or tombstoned-closed makes `reduce_ticket` return None (status ""), so it is classified as still-open and listed as a blocker, contradicting the docstring's claim of using "the same open-vs-closed rule build_dep_graph uses".
scenarios: An `open` subject with two prerequisites, one genuinely open and one archived/tombstoned-away: the reason string and `blockers` detail falsely include the tombstoned prerequisite as an open blocker.
Operator reads the not-claimable finding and chases a prerequisite that is actually already closed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Filter blockers via `rebar.graph._status._get_ticket_status(bid, tracker)` (which handles missing dirs and `.tombstone.json`) instead of raw `reduce_ticket`, keeping the same `not in ("closed","deleted")` test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Default `runner` to a non-null string (e.g. `getattr(cfg, "runner", "") or ""`) so the early-return verdict always satisfies the schema's string-typed `runner`.
evidence: claimability.py:160: `"runner": getattr(cfg, "runner", None),`
claimability.py:165-167: `return findings.validate_structured(verdict, "plan_review_verdict")`
src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json:73: `"runner": { "type": "string", ... }` (model allows null at line 74, runner does not)
advisory.finding: `indeterminate_verdict` stamps `runner` via `getattr(cfg, "runner", None)`, but the `plan_review_verdict` schema declares `runner` as `type: "string"` (no null); a missing/None `cfg.runner` would produce `runner: null` and fail `findings.validate_structured`. Only the `LLMConfig.runner` default of "pydantic_ai" keeps this latent.
scenarios: A caller passes a `cfg` lacking a `runner` attribute (or an explicit None), turning the fast-fail into a `FindingsError` instead of a clean INDETERMINATE.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `getattr(cfg, "runner", "") or ""` for `runner` (model may stay nullable).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `review-plan` on a `closed` task fast-fails to INDETERMINATE with `coverage.llm_ran=false` and finding `ticket-not-claimable` (status == "closed"), mirroring the blocked/idea tests.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:34: `_NOT_CLAIMABLE_STATUSES = frozenset({"closed", "idea", "blocked"})`
search for `closed` in test_plan_policy_dogfood.py returned no matches — only blocked (line 181) and idea (line 193) status tests exist
docs/plan-review-gate.md:45 and AGENTS.md list `closed` as a first-class fast-fail status, yet no test covers it
advisory.finding: The `closed` status fast-fail path is untested. `_NOT_CLAIMABLE_STATUSES` includes `"closed"` and the docs advertise closed as a fast-fail trigger, but the dogfood suite only exercises `blocked`, `idea`, and open-prerequisite. Removing `"closed"` from the frozenset (or mis-handling a closed-then-re-review) would pass all tests — a regression-blindness gap for a distinct, documented trigger.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_closed_status_ticket_fast_fails_without_llm` that creates a task, transitions it to `closed`, runs `review_plan` with `_BoomRunner()`, asserts `_assert_not_claimable(...)` and `result["indeterminate"][0]["status"] == "closed"`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs `review-plan` on a not-claimable ticket via the real CLI and asserts stdout contains the `[indeterminate ticket-not-claimable] <reason>` line and the `→ <remediation>` line.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:600-604: `for f in result.get("indeterminate", []): ... sys.stdout.write(f"  [indeterminate {f.get('id', '')}] {reason}\n") ... sys.stdout.write(f"    → {f['remediation']}\n")`
The commit message states 'The CLI now surfaces each indeterminate finding's reason + remediation' — a claimed observable behavior
No test in tests/ asserts the `[indeterminate` output string or the `→` remediation line (searches for the surfacing loop turned up no CLI-output assertion)
advisory.finding: The new CLI loop that surfaces each indeterminate finding's reason + remediation (the user-facing product of this change on the CLI) has no test. No test asserts that a not-claimable fast-fail (or snapshot-collection error) prints the `[indeterminate <id>] <reason>` line and the `→ <remediation>` line to stdout, so a regression that drops or malforms this output would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_plan_policy_dogfood.py use `_cli(rebar_repo, "review-plan", subject)` against a link-blocked ticket and assert `"[indeterminate ticket-not-claimable]"` and `"→"` appear in `result.stdout` (and exit code 2).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches `deps_state` (or `reduce_ticket`) to raise and asserts `not_claimable_verdict` returns `None` so the full review proceeds (fail-open).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:52-55: `try: graph = deps_state(...) except Exception: ... return None`
claimability.py:18-20 docstring: 'Fail-OPEN throughout: any error computing claimability yields None (the full review proceeds and surfaces real errors)'
No dedicated test for claimability.py exists (search for `claimability` under tests/ returned no matches)
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:62-63: `if ticket_type not in _REVIEWED_TYPES: return None`
claimability.py:14-16 documents bug/session_log exemption as intentional
No test creates a bug/session_log and asserts it is NOT fast-failed by the claimability gate
advisory.finding: The module's stated fail-open safety invariant is untested. `not_claimable_verdict` returns `None` (letting the full review proceed) on any exception from `deps_state` or `reduce_ticket`, and the docstring calls this 'Fail-OPEN throughout ... so a precheck fault never suppresses a legitimate review.' No test injects a precheck fault to prove the full review still runs — a regression that swallowed a real review here would be invisible.
merged_from: The type-exemption branch (`ticket_type not in _REVIEWED_TYPES -> return None`) for `bug`/`session_log` is untested. The design deliberately does not fast-fail these types; a regression that fast-failed a non-claimable bug (instead of the exempt PASS) would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the review_plan not-claimable fast-fail (previously-valid inputs now returning INDETERMINATE/exit 2) is an intended, acceptably-mitigated behavior change on the public CLI/library/MCP surface, given the documented --force/force=True migration path.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:521-524: `if not force: not_claimable = claimability.not_claimable_verdict(...); if not_claimable is not None: return not_claimable` — short-circuits before any review
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:70-79: statuses closed/idea/blocked and `open` with ready_to_work false now yield an INDETERMINATE verdict

tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py:255-257: a pre-existing test that reviewed a link-blocked open ticket had to add `force=True` (`# a default review would fast-fail as not-yet-claimable`) — proves existing PASS flows now diverge

tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py:291-295, 358-366, 418-425, 568-573, 591-596, 620-626, 637-643: seven further existing review calls retrofitted with force=True for the same reason

Migration path IS provided and documented: --force (CLI, _cli/_llm_commands.py:465-470) and force=True (library/MCP, _mcp_llm.py:199-204) bypass the gate; docs updated across plan-review-gate.md/user-guide.md/exit-codes.md
advisory.finding: review_plan changes its default behavior on previously-valid inputs: an `open` ticket blocked by an unclosed dependency (ready_to_work=false) and closed/idea/blocked tickets now fast-fail to INDETERMINATE (exit 2) instead of running the review and returning PASS/BLOCK. This narrows the accepted input of the public `rebar review-plan` CLI, the rebar.llm.review_plan library API, and the MCP review_plan tool without a version gate; existing callers must now pass --force/force=True to get the prior behavior.
scenarios: An existing script or CI job that runs `rebar review-plan <id>` on a ticket ahead of closing its prerequisites now gets exit 2 / INDETERMINATE where it previously got a PASS/BLOCK verdict
A programmatic caller of rebar.llm.review_plan on a blocked/idea ticket now receives INDETERMINATE with coverage.llm_ran=false instead of a real review
